summary.intent: Use the GSD manager to drive milestone v2.0 (cipher-box) to completion — verify/discuss/plan/execute remaining phases, keep multi-hour autonomous work resuming across quota resets via cron, and ship Phase 74 through the full ship-phase pipeline.
summary.outcome: Phase 70.1 was verified (SC#6 live crash-resume suite passed 6/6) and Phase 69's false 'Executing' status was root-caused and fixed; both shipped via PR #606 merged to main. Phases 74, 75, and 77 were subsequently planned and executed on separate feat branches across several quota-interrupted, cron-resumed sessions (75 and 77 fully verifier-passed/complete; 74 code-verified with only CI-gated Windows/desktop-e2e legs outstanding). Phase 76 was halted by the user before work began; 78/79 remain untouched. At transcript end, the user had switched to feat/74 and invoked /ship-phase 74, which was mid-pipeline (canonicalizing verification) when the transcript ends.

repo: gsd-tools' plan-scan.cjs has a loose fallback that counts ANY .md file whose name merely contains the substring 'PLAN' (case-insensitive) as a plan file — a doc named '*-WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md' was miscounted as a 26th plan, making plan_count(26) > summary_count(25) and flipping a 100%-complete phase to disk_status 'partial' (dashboard shows '◆ Executing').

Manager's is_active flag just means 'a file in the phase dir was modified in the last 5 minutes' — it does NOT mean an agent is actually running; touching any file (even an unrelated UAT stub) flips it true.

verify-work's 'phase uat-passed --require-verification' predicate downgrades a phase with implementation done + verification passed but no UAT.md to not-fully-complete — phases verified by CI/cargo only (no human UAT) need a UAT.md stub written explicitly, or the predicate blocks completion (same class of gap seen with phase 70.1's human_needed state).

vitest does not load .env files, so SDK_E2E_SECRET must be exported manually into the shell before running sdk-e2e suites; otherwise the harness falls back to a hardcoded default secret and gets 401 from the API, which looks like a code failure but isn't.

The API process on :3000 can silently be a stale `node dist/main.js` build (detached, PPID 1) serving old code with a mismatched TEST_LOGIN_SECRET; must verify PID/start-time and restart from source (`pnpm --filter api dev` / `nest start --watch`) before trusting live-stack test results.

commit.gpgsign=false in this repo, so autonomous/unattended commits don't block on 1Password biometric prompts; pre-commit hooks (lint-staged) are just slow (~1-2 min), and the gsd commit helper can false-negative 'commit_failed' while the commit actually landed — always verify via `git log` before retrying.

Sub-agents spawned at the repo root cannot use EnterWorktree to pin into an already-existing worktree (errors 'repo root, not an isolated worktree') — the working pattern for background-planned-then-executed phases is sequential processing on the main checkout, switching branches per phase.
gsd-plan-phase can create a stray `docs/plan-phase-<N>` branch and leave `<N>-PATTERNS.md` untracked — must be reconciled onto the phase's `feat/*` branch and committed explicitly.
CodeRabbit bundles nitpicks in the PR review body rather than inline threads (confirmed again this session), consistent with prior memory.

code.finding: Loose `/PLAN/i` substring fallback matcher miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. 'WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md') as a phase plan file, corrupting plan_count vs summary_count comparisons used for completion status.
`is_active` is computed purely from 'file modified in phase dir within last 5 minutes', not from any actual process/agent liveness signal.

workflow: When a background/worktree agent dies mid-task on a quota limit, its task-notification summary can understate progress — always re-assess the actual on-disk git state (branches, commits, plan files) rather than trusting the truncated final message.

For autonomous multi-phase execution that may span quota resets, schedule a CronCreate 'safety-net' resume ~5h out (next reset) each time — but the resume prompt must be corrected/re-issued whenever the working method changes (e.g. after abandoning worktree-based EnterWorktree for sequential main-checkout), or stale instructions get replayed on the next auto-resume.

Instruct autonomous sub-agents to run pipeline steps synchronously rather than writing their own background-wait loops — a self-made wait loop caused one agent to stall and return prematurely with no real progress.

Before rerunning a large multi-gate pipeline (ship-phase: verify/secure/validate/simplify/e2e/coderabbit/ship), first inventory which gate artifacts already exist and are satisfied (e.g. Validation already compliant, commit subjects already conventional) to avoid redoing satisfied steps.

Treat CI-only verification legs (Windows-only compile, multi-platform desktop-e2e) as infra-gated rather than human_needed/code gaps when the host OS can't run them locally — canonicalize verification status and record the CI dependency in the phase's UAT.md.

friction: Multiple session quota-limit interruptions ('You've hit your session limit') during long parallel planning/execution runs, requiring cron-scheduled autonomous resumes and careful state reconstruction each time.

Phase 69's false 'Executing' status required a long multi-step root-cause chase (UAT gap theory, then plan-count mismatch, then resolver internals) before finding the real plan-scan.cjs substring bug.
EnterWorktree failed when sub-agents tried to pin into pre-existing worktrees, wasting a launch cycle and forcing a mid-run pivot to sequential main-checkout-per-branch.
Stale API process on :3000 (old dist build, wrong secret) produced a misleading 401 that looked like a Phase 70.1 code defect.

vitest not loading .env caused a second, distinct false-failure signal (401 again) even after the API was correctly restarted from source, requiring further diagnosis to find the missing exported secret.
One background planning/execution agent stalled in a self-authored background wait loop and had to be relaunched.
A stale rust-analyzer E0277 diagnostic in an agent's report looked like a compile regression and required an independent `cargo check --workspace` to rule out.
Uncommitted planning-doc changes piled up on `main` (commit-to-main forbidden by user's rules), requiring a branch+PR detour mid-flow to unblock further work.
User had to manually interrupt/stop the Phase 76 agent to pause the autonomous cascade.
